title: ArduinoOTA: upload firmware to a board over Wi-Fi

spans.text: This example uploads from Arduino IDE to a supported ESP32 on the same Wi-Fi network. The first setup still needs USB: install a sketch with Wi-Fi and OTA support over the cable, then later uploads can use the network.
to process the transfer. The board should appear as a network port in the IDE. Select the same network and the correct board/core. Long

calls or blocking sensor code can interrupt OTA handling.

This is an Arduino-ESP32-style example;
and ArduinoOTA are not available on every Arduino board. Wi-Fi-enabled MKR and other boards may use a different API, so follow their board documentation.

spans.title: Important note
spans.text: Replace Wi-Fi placeholders locally; never commit credentials. Configure ArduinoOTA authentication and do not expose unauthenticated updates on an untrusted network. Require secure transport and image verification in production.
